St. Michael's C.E. Middle School
‘Each person, uniquely made in God’s image, merits the best that we can give’.
Our sense of purpose begins with the above quote from our mission statement, rooted in the highest possible notion of young people. All that we do flows from this including our core values of Aspiration, Belief and Creativity: St Michael’s ABC.
Our pupils join St Michael’s at a crucial stage of transition from childhood to early adulthood. We support them through this journey in three key ways. Firstly, by inspiring them to aim high in all areas of schooling and personal development. In addition to this we coach pupils to sustain belief in all situations and challenges. Finally, we actively seek ways to for all pupils to explore and nurture their creativity.
We hope this website gives you an insight into what makes St Michael’s special and we would be delighted to meet you and show you the school in more detail.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Michael's C.E. Middle School - French Trip - Day 2
pageCache.text:
St. Michael's C.E. Middle School
News and Events
Latest News
French Trip - Day 2
We have had a lovely first full day in France. It has been a busy day and the weather has been great!
We visited the local school where students had a chance to practice their French. The school took us to a small château where we had our lunch, then a look round an exhibition dedicated to Cecil Newton, the British soldier the school is named after. As the sun came out, we made an impromptu trip to the beach and a stop for ice cream.
We are now heading back to the Château du Baffy for our evening meal and some evening activities.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Michael's C.E. Middle School - Holne Park 2026 - Day 4 and Return Information
pageCache.text:
St. Michael's C.E. Middle School
News and Events
Latest News
Holne Park 2026 - Day 4 and Return Information
Pupils had a good Day 4 at Holne Park and completed their cycle of activities for the day. Mrs. Prosser returned from the trip yesterday and commented on how many children had taken themselves out of their comfort zone, pushed through fears and worries and completed activities such as high ropes and caving (including squeezing through the legendary cheese press rocks in the cave).
Pupils have now packed up their belongings and are completing the final activities for the day, have a chance to review the week and have some lunch before setting off back to school. A reminder to all parents that the estimated time of arrival back at school is 5pm (depending upon traffic through Devon which is always variable). If we are expecting any significant deviation from this time, this will be communicated to all parents via Arbor. PLEASE do not park in the areas where buses need to pull up at the front of school. The car park of the school will be open from 4.45pm for parents to use for parking to keep the road clear.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Michael's C.E. Middle School - MP Vikki Slade visits St. Michael's
pageCache.text:
St. Michael's C.E. Middle School
News and Events
Latest News
MP Vikki Slade visits St. Michael's
We were delighted to welcome our local MP, Vikki, to St. Michael’s last week. Vikki has visited every school in her constituency since being elected and takes a close, active interest in education.
She started her visit with a tour of the campus, guided by three of our Year 8 school ambassadors. Together, they spent time exploring some of the highly creative subjects offered at St. Michael's, including art, design technology, and music.
Following the tour, Vikki met with our school council to answer their questions. The conversation was incredibly engaging, with topics ranging from how one becomes an MP and how to build the confidence to speak with high-profile figures, to whether she has aspirations of becoming Prime Minister! The school council also sought her advice on how to take action to improve road safety directly outside the school gates.
We would all like to extend our warmest thanks to Vikki for taking the time to visit St. Michael’s and inspire our pupils.

After a big full-cooked breakfast, pupils headed out for lots of activities. We managed to get lots of nervous children through the cave today, and they can be very proud of their resilience. Hot dogs for lunch and more fun in the afternoon with some excellent attempts on the high ropes before our roast turkey dinner and sticky toffee pudding. More evening activities and then a slightly earlier night, so rest and recover ahead of another busy day tomorrow.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Michael's C.E. Middle School - St Michael’s Middle School Strikes Platinum Again with Prestigious School Games Mark Award
pageCache.text:
St. Michael's C.E. Middle School
News and Events
Latest News
St Michael’s Middle School Strikes Platinum Again with Prestigious School Games Mark Award
St Michael’s CE Middle School is celebrating once again after retaining the prestigious School Games Platinum Mark, the highest possible government-led accolade for school sports provision.
Facilitated by the Youth Sport Trust, the Platinum award is reserved exclusively for schools demonstrating a long-term commitment to high-quality physical education, inclusive competition, and outstanding leadership. St Michael's stood out for its exceptional student engagement, with over 50% of pupils regularly participating in extra-curricular sports as well as its diverse curriculum, which utilises the school's on-site swimming pool and offers unique activities ranging from traditional rugby and netball to parkour and handball. This consecutive achievement highlights the school's ongoing dedication to fostering healthy lifestyles, teamwork, and sportsmanship across all year groups.

pageCache.text:
St. Michael's C.E. Middle School
News and Events
Latest News
French Trip - Day 3
Here is the update for day 3 of the Year 8 French residential trip.
We made the most of the amazing weather today. Students used their French to barter in the market at Bayeux. We then went on to Arromaches to visit the D-Day 360 cinema and town before a very calm and respectful time at the American cemetery and memorial.

pageCache.pageTitle: St. Michael's C.E. Middle School - French Trip - Day 4
pageCache.text:
St. Michael's C.E. Middle School
News and Events
Latest News
French Trip - Day 4
Our last full day in France and a busy day when we get to visit one of the highlights of the trip.
Up early and straight to the caramel factory. We suspect that some of you may receive presents from there. Unless they get eaten! We then made our way to Mont Saint-Michel, walking along the causeway and up to the top to take in the amazing views before an ice cream, for those who wanted one, and the walk back. Back to the château tonight and packing up in the morning, ready for the journey home.
Pegasus bridge tomorrow then a trip to a hypermarket and the ferry home.

pageCache.text:
St. Michael's C.E. Middle School
Learning
Careers guidance & how to get involved.
Careers guidance & how to get involved.
Careers Guidance Aims
By using the Gatsby benchmarks, we are committed to ensuring that pupils are well-informed and equipped to make decisions regarding their future by the time they leave for their upper school education. Our aim is that by the time they leave us, every student at St Michael’s should recognise and have knowledge of their own strengths and be able to link these qualities to possible future education and career opportunities.
Why consider careers at middle school age?
Students have to make decisions on GCSE options in Year 9 - their first year in upper school. We want to prepare students for these decisions in good time, so they have time to reflect on their options.
Students who have thought about their possible career destination are more likely to be motivated to work their best and achieve in their chosen area.
Even for those who do not wish to make choices yet, considering their future prospects encourages students to take responsibility for their learning and to have discussions about their future with parents or carers.
Students and Parents/Carers Please enjoy exploring our careers pages using the tabs to discover useful websites and to see our trust careers policies as well as our own programmes and aims at St Michael’s. Our newsletters are the best way to see all the fantastic opportunities our pupils have been experiencing.
You can explore career opportunities as a student or with your parents by visiting the careers websites page. Have you explored what jobs might be out there in the future!
If you have any comments or feedback on the St Michael’s careers programme or on the information provided, please let us know – contact details below.
